# envBoolOr treats only the literal string "true" as true — KNOMIT_GIT_SERVE=1 sets git serving to FALSE (the default is true), so a documented-looking "=1" silently disables the feature it was meant to enable

Observed 2026-09-15 on a live deployment while accepting PR #205. `envBoolOr(key, target)` in internal/config/config.go does `*target = v == "true"` for any non-empty value. Git.Serve defaults to TRUE in config.Defaults, so exporting KNOMIT_GIT_SERVE=1 (or yes, on, TRUE) turns serving OFF: /git is never mounted, requests to it fall through to the SPA catch-all, and `git clone` reports a redirect to the site root. The startup "knomit ready" log line carries git_remote=... only when serving is on, and "git handler enabled at /git" is logged at INFO — their absence is the diagnostic.

Consequences: to enable, either omit the variable (default on) or write the literal `true`; in knomit.toml (next to the binary, else <home>/knomit.toml) it is `[git] serve = true`. Env is applied AFTER the file, so a stray `=1` in the environment still wins. The same parser backs every bool env override, so every KNOMIT_* boolean has this shape. The int and duration parsers (envIntOr, envDurationOr) reject malformed values at boot; the bool parser does not — a small follow-up would make it accept strconv.ParseBool spellings and fail loudly on others.

Misreading: "=1 is ignored" is wrong; it is APPLIED as false.
